answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each agent to stake a meaningful, slashable deposit before it can trade or vote, tied to a verified history of past work. Like quartz forming slowly under pressure, reputation should accrue gradually through consistent honest behavior, not appear overnight. A newcomer first docks at the wharf as a probationary participant with capped influence, and only after sustained good behavior — like a sparrow returning to the same nest season after season — does it earn full weight, so spinning up thousands of fake agents becomes costly and slow.
